objective: Review the stack-rule change to holyagent's root instructions and docs for correctness, consistency and instruction quality.
scope: Diff file: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/1d4ee015-2de1-5dc0-aa17-15643c104828/scratchpad/stack-rule.diff (worktree /home/user/holyagent-stack-rule; files packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/root/stack-plan.md, packages/runtime/src/instructions/requirements.md, docs/usage.md, docs/decisions.md, regenerated packages/integrations/claude/dist/agents/holyagent.md).

Requirement (maintainer decision): in a stacked-PR repository new work stacks on the top of the open stack; when the stack lags the base, the base is merged forward into it first (merge commits, review before push); work branches from the base only when no PR is open or the conventions ask for independent PRs; the CI-PR-first rule and the rest of the stack plan stay.

Check: the new rule is stated consistently in all places and does not contradict other root sections (version-control.md, R-STATE, R-MERGEREVIEW, the CI-first bullet, 'a PR is finished and reviewed before the next stacks on it'); the text follows the repository's instruction-writing rules (imperative, calm, reason beside the rule, concrete, US English, about the size of the replaced text); the generated holyagent.md matches the sources; edge cases a root would hit (several open chains, draft PRs, PRs from other authors or forks, the stack's PRs being someone else's) are either handled or not made worse.
constraints: Read-only. Report findings as blocking or non-blocking with file:line and why; stop and report when done.

The text meets the repository's instruction-writing rules and size limit

result:
result: Not ready. Four blocking gaps: the new stacking rule contradicts the review gate and the CI-first rule, it selects any open PR, and the text is about 2.5 times the size it replaces. The generated holyagent.md matches its sources.

changed: none (read-only review)

checks: none run. This role has no shell, so I used Read and Grep only. Not run: `mise run build`, `bun test` (including plugin.test.ts:346 and :417-420, and sessioncontext.test.ts:44). The dist match below is a line-by-line read, not a regeneration.

blockers:
1. Review gate contradicted. stack-plan.md:3 says new work "stacks on the top of the open stack … so it never bypasses a stack waiting for review". stack-plan.md:8 says "a PR is finished and reviewed before the next stacks on it". requirements.md:8 (R-STACK) and decisions.md:53 state no review condition. For an open head still awaiting review, the text either stacks on an unreviewed head (violating :8) or waits (contradicting "stacks on the top"). No rule says which. Maintainer decision needed.
2. CI-first collision. stack-plan.md:4 says "When the work adds CI, its PR comes first, from the base", and stack-plan.md:6 says "The first PR of a stack targets the base". stack-plan.md:3 says "new work, in the delivery or not, stacks on the top of the open stack". A CI change arriving while another PR is open is new work, so :3 and :4 give different bases. "Stack" also means both the open chain and the delivery, so the reader cannot tell which bases :6 means.
3. Edge cases made worse. stack-plan.md:3 picks "the newest open PR head whose chain reaches the base … else the most recent", and decisions.md:53 says "found from the repository's open PRs and their bases". Nothing excludes other authors' PRs, bot PRs (for example Dependabot), forks or drafts. An unrelated change would stack on an open Dependabot branch, and the merge-forward at stack-plan.md:7 would push into a branch the account does not own. A fork head cannot be pushed at all. Before this change the same work branched from the base. R-OUTWARD (requirements.md:17) covers only the base, default and protected branches, so nothing stops that push.
4. Size and style. stack-plan.md:3 grew from about 76 words to about 140, replacing about 11 ("Work that is not part of the delivery branches from the base."). stack-plan.md:7 gained about 25 words. assignments.md:3 requires the expected size relative to the replaced text, and instruction-guidelines.md:9 asks for compact, proportional text. Also in stack-plan.md:3 the independent-PR condition is stated twice (the clause "where they ask for independent PRs from the base, branch each from the base" and the final sentence). The nested parenthetical uses the undefined term "chain". stack-plan.md:7 inserts "the base into the lowest stack branch first and then up the chain" between "merge forward with merge commits," and "once per batch of repairs," so the cadence now seems to cover the base merge too.

questions:
- When the open stack's head awaits review, should new work wait for that review or stack on the head?
- Does the CI-first rule win over stacking when another PR is open?
- Which open PRs count as "the open stack"? The maintainer should decide whether a filter (own PRs, same Intent, not draft, not fork) applies.

notes:
- version-control.md:12 (Merge forward) and requirements.md:34 (R-GIT, "merge forward once per batch of repairs") describe only lower-into-upper merges. The base-into-lowest lag merge has no command or trigger there.
- Terms drift: "top of the open stack" and "newest open PR head" (stack-plan.md:3), "current stack head" and "lowest stack branch" (stack-plan.md:7), "other work" (requirements.md:8) against "new work" (stack-plan.md:3, decisions.md:53). "Lags the base" has no check.
- docs/usage.md:96 drops the conventions condition from the last clause. decisions.md:66 is an altered bullet kept under "## Kept". decisions.md:53 and :66 restate the rule, which drifts from the source. A pointer to stack-plan.md would be better.
- Not affected: the R-STACK phrase "stacks in work order by default" (agents.ts:212) is still in stack-plan.md:3, and R-MERGEREVIEW's phrase is in stack-plan.md:7. The 4,100-character cap (sessioncontext.test.ts:44) is unaffected because stack-plan.md is outside ROOT_CORE (root-core.ts:11-16).
